references.text: The parallel passage in Exodus where the third commandment was first given, with identical wording about not misusing the Lord's name.
Prohibits swearing falsely by God's name, which is a form of misusing his name.
Describes the punishment for one who blasphemes the Lord's name, emphasizing the seriousness of dishonoring God's name.
Speaks of enemies who misuse God's name and shows the consequences of such actions.
A prayer not to profane God's name, showing reverence for keeping his name holy.
God rebukes Israel for profaning his name among the nations.
Jesus expands on the commandment by teaching not to swear at all, but to let your 'yes' be yes and your 'no' be no.
The Lord's Prayer begins with 'Hallowed be your name,' which is the positive side of this commandment.
James warns against swearing but encourages honesty in speech, in line with respect for God's name.
